1.
Learned counsel for the petitioner state that all petitions are identical.
2. This is a batch of petitions where similar questions of law and facts are involved.

The prayers made in the petitions are also identical, which arise out of acquisition of lands belonging to the petitioners for the National Highway Project under the provisions of National Highway Act, 1956.

There is no dispute in regard to the notifications pertaining to the acquisitions of the land in question, as also the acquisition culminating into a final award and possession of petitioners'
lands being taken over for the purpose of national highway project.

sentences.text: The common grievance of the petitioners is in regard to non-payment of statutory benefits of solatium and interest, as would be applicable even in respect of acquisition proceedings under the National Highway Act by applying the provisions of Section 23(2), Section 23(1)(A) by providing 12% interest as well as interest as provided under Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

The prayers in all these petitions being similar, for convenience we refer to the prayers made in the first petition being Writ Petition No.13634 of 2025, which read thus :
 "(a) Issue appropriate Writ / Order for directing the Respondents to
immediately

grant amount of Solatium @ 30% along with interest in  addition to the amount of compensation, with regard to the land belonging  to the Petitioner having an area admeasuring 550 sq. mtrs. from Survey  No.88/2 situated at Village Velholi Taluka and District Nashik, in  accordance with law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Union of  India v. Tarsem Singh (2019) 9 SCC 304 case, which is followed by the  Divisional Benches of this Hon'ble High Court, (which are annexed at  Exhibit-"C" Collectively)."

entities.text: Union of  India v. Tarsem Singh (2019) 9 SCC 304
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Tarsem Singh and others1, in which the Supreme Court had declared that the provisions of Land Acquisition Act relating to solatium and interest contained in Sections 23(1-A) and (2) and interest payable in terms of proviso below Section 28 shall apply to acquisitions made under the National Highways Act (for short Kaliya Exports Thr Porp Tribhuvandas ... vs Union Of India Thr Its Deputy Secretary ... on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93966777/

The request is rejected."

opennyai_summary.facts:
The prayers made in the petitions are also identical, which arise out of acquisition of lands belonging to the petitioners for the National Highway Project under the provisions of National Highway Act, 1956.
There is no dispute in regard to the notifications pertaining to the acquisitions of the land in question, as also the acquisition culminating into a final award and possession of petitioners'
lands being taken over for the purpose of national highway project.
The common grievance of the petitioners is in regard to non-payment of statutory benefits of solatium and interest, as would be applicable even in respect of acquisition proceedings under the National Highway Act by applying the provisions of Section 23(2), Section 23(1)(A) by providing 12% interest as well as interest as provided under Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
